svg.aria-label: WFDB-x: the WFDB package in seven languages, how to get it, how it is verified against the original, and what it adds
svg.text: The WFDB Software Package for physiologic signals, in Python, C++, Rust, Julia, R, MATLAB/Octave and Kotlin.
The complete package, in every language.

text.tspan: under their C names: isigopen, getvec, getann …
with the same options, output, messages and exit status.
FLAC included; multi-segment, multi-frequency, remote records.

svg.text: Each language has its own complete package: no C library and no other language needed.
IN YOUR CODE: READ A RECORD

URL and turn network access on. The same
two settings work in every language.

svg.text: $ in a shell; julia> and >> in Julia and MATLAB/Octave. wfdbx launches the tools (in Julia, R and Octave: an alias, see the README).
In your code, every language also offers the C-style functions under their C names (isigopen, getvec, …).
Same results as the original, verified
Every tool in every language runs the same test cases and must match the original C programs.

text.tspan: is checked the same way, against the unmodified C programs (877 cases).
are listed in docs/DIVERGENCES.md and tested like everything else.
in each language check the library and the high-level API.
